place.zh: 石坳村 · 家中 · 天未亮

setup.zh: 立冬这天，天还没亮。娘卸下一条鹿后腿，斩作两截，埋进腌芥菜的缸底，拿草绳把缸绑在你背上：「给吴婆婆送一缸腌菜去。走屋后头，别走井台。趁天没亮。」
setup.en: The Start of Winter, before dawn. Your mother takes off a hind leg of the deer, chops it in two, buries it at the bottom of the vat of pickled mustard greens, and ties the vat to your back with straw rope: "Take Granny Wu a vat of pickles. Go round the back of the house, not past the well. While it's still dark."

recap.zh: 立冬天没亮，你背着一缸「腌菜」从屋后头绕过井台，给吴婆婆送去了鹿腿——她说是你爹在山涧边上答应的。然后她朝你肩上看不见的银光，慢慢低下了头。
recap.en: Before dawn on the Start of Winter you carried a vat of "pickles" on your back round behind the houses, past the well, and brought Granny Wu the leg of venison — your father promised it, she said, by the mountain stream. Then she slowly bowed her head toward the silver on your shoulder she could not see.

zh: 一缸腌菜，芥菜底下埋着一条鹿腿。
她朝着那团看不见的银光，低下了头。
en: A vat of pickles; under the mustard greens, a leg of venison.
"The venison's come? Your father promised it."
She bows her head toward a silver light she cannot see.

story.zh:
立冬这天，是九月十五——那一年闰了个八月，节气赶在了前头，九月半便立了冬。天还没亮，小满是给他娘剁骨头的声音吵醒的。

「咚。咚。咚。」一声一声，又沉又稳。他爬起来往灶间一看，只见他娘挽着袖子，拿他爹那把剥皮的短刀，顺着骨缝一刀一刀地走，走到关节那里，手腕一翻，「喀」的一声，一整条鹿后腿便卸了下来。他爹蹲在一旁看着，张着嘴，看了半天，道：「……你什么时候学的？」他娘道：「『[依乎天理，批大郤，导大窾，因其固然。]{典=zhuangzi-paoding}』顺着缝走，刀就不碰骨头。」

她到炕头打开那只木箱，翻出一块包腿的布来。翻的时候，她把箱底一个巴掌大的旧布包拿起来，搁在一边；找着了布，又把那个布包放回了原处，放得很轻，轻得像放一个睡着了的孩子。布包里，是那只碗的七八片。

她在膝弯那里又下了一刀，把鹿腿斩作两截，拿布包了，揭开墙角那只腌芥菜疙瘩的缸，把两截鹿腿埋进芥菜底下，一层一层压实了，盖上木盖。小满道：「娘，鹿腿也能腌？」他娘道：「能腌。」小满道：「好吃吗？」他娘道：「不知道。没腌过。」说着拿草绳把那只缸捆了，往他背上一绑，道：「给吴婆婆送一缸腌菜去。走屋后头，别走井台。趁天没亮。」

小满背着缸出门的时候，他娘已把剩下的肉、皮、角、下水，都在院子里摊开了，摊得整整齐齐，那一挂下水，偏偏摆在最当门的地方。然后她洗了手，把袖子放下来，坐在门槛里头，静静地等着。
story.en:
The first day of winter fell on the fifteenth of the ninth month that year — there'd been a leap eighth month, so the seasons ran ahead, and winter began in the middle of the ninth. Before it was light, Xiaoman was woken by the sound of his mother chopping bones.

*Thock. Thock. Thock.* One stroke after another, heavy and steady. He got up and looked into the kitchen. There was his mother, sleeves rolled up, working his father's short skinning knife down the seams between the bones, cut by cut, and when she reached the joint she turned her wrist, there was a *crack*, and a whole hind leg of deer came away. His father crouched beside her watching with his mouth open, watched a long time, and said, "…When did you learn that?" His mother said, "'[Follow the natural lines, strike in the big gaps, guide the blade through the big hollows, go by how it is made.]{典=zhuangzi-paoding}' Go along the seams and the knife never touches bone."

She went to the head of the bed, opened the wooden chest, and rummaged for a cloth to wrap the leg in. As she rummaged she lifted out a palm-sized bundle of old cloth from the bottom of the chest and put it to one side; when she'd found the cloth she put the bundle back where it had been, very gently, as gently as laying down a sleeping child. In the bundle were the seven or eight pieces of that bowl.

She cut again at the bend of the knee and split the leg in two, wrapped the pieces in the cloth, took the lid off the crock of pickled mustard root in the corner, buried the two pieces of leg under the mustard, pressed it down firm layer by layer, and put the wooden lid back on. Xiaoman said, "Ma, can you pickle deer leg too?" His mother said, "You can pickle it." Xiaoman said, "Does it taste good?" His mother said, "Don't know. Never pickled one." She bound the crock with straw rope and tied it onto his back. "Take Granny Wu a crock of pickles. Go round the back of the houses, not past the well. While it's still dark."

When Xiaoman went out with the crock on his back, his mother had already laid out the rest of the meat, the hide, the antlers and the offal in the yard, all laid out very neatly — and the string of offal, of all things, right in front of the door. Then she washed her hands, let her sleeves down, sat inside the threshold, and waited quietly.

exits.means: takes the jar of venison to Granny Wu before dawn, round the back

story.zh:
村东头那户，吴婆婆已经坐在门槛上了，脸朝着东边那一线鱼肚白。小满还没开口，她已道：「鹿腿来了？」

他娘一个字也没提鹿腿。吴婆婆道：「你爹答应的。在山涧边上，蹲着摸那个蹄印的时候。」那山涧在黑松岭里头，离这门槛少说也有三四十里地。她露出那三颗牙来，笑了：「我耳朵好。」说着拍了拍门槛：「坐下吧。」

小满便坐下了。吴婆婆朝着村外的坡田抽了抽鼻子，自言自语地道：「婆婆小时候，开春一锄头翻下去，那土是甜丝丝的。那时候，这地，是香的。」说完便不说话了，伸出那只枯瘦的手来摸他的头，摸到他脖子上那条「围脖」，手便停住了，一动也不动，好像生怕一动，便会把什么东西惊醒了。

然后她把手收回去，朝着那团谁都看不见的银光，很慢、很慢地低下了头，低得几乎到了膝盖上，又慢慢地抬起来，脸上什么表情也没有。

「回罢。日头上来了，马家的人，也该到了。」
story.en:
At the house at the east end of the village, Granny Wu was already sitting on her doorstep, her face to the thin fish-belly white in the east. Before Xiaoman could open his mouth she said, "The deer leg's come?"

His mother hadn't said a word about any deer leg. Granny Wu said, "Your father promised it. By the mountain stream, crouching there touching that hoof print." That stream was inside Black Pine Ridge, a good thirty or forty li from this doorstep. She showed her three teeth and laughed. "I've got good ears." She patted the doorstep. "Sit down."

So Xiaoman sat. Granny Wu sniffed in the direction of the hill fields outside the village and said to herself, "When Granny was little, come spring, you turned the soil with one stroke of the hoe and it smelled sweet. Back then, this land smelled good." With that she fell silent, and reached out her bony hand to touch his head. When it came to the "scarf" round his neck, her hand stopped, perfectly still, as if afraid that if it moved it would wake something.

Then she drew her hand back, and towards that patch of silver light nobody could see she bowed her head, very, very slowly, so low it almost touched her knees, and slowly raised it again, without any expression on her face at all.

"Off you go. The sun's coming up. The Ma people will be along."

label.en: Stay in and watch over it

exits.means: stays home with the fox that morning instead of going

story.zh:
那缸腌菜，是他爹送去的。他爹瘸着腿去了，瘸着腿回来，说吴婆婆接了缸，揭开盖子闻了闻，什么也没说，只朝着他们家这边，坐了好一会儿。

小满没出门。他守着怀里那团凉冰冰的银毛，数了三遍它还在不在喘气。日头上来了，马家的人，也该到了。
story.en:
It was his father who took the crock over. He limped there and limped back, and said Granny Wu took the crock, lifted the lid and sniffed, and said not a word, only sat facing their house for a good while.

Xiaoman stayed in. He watched over the cold silver fur inside his jacket, and three times counted whether it was still breathing. The sun was up; the Mas would be coming.
